domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk's core technical content centers on multi-agent swarm architecture with thousands of parallel tool calls and novel agentic control flow for autonomous troubleshooting. The product is deployed in enterprise operations environments for production incident response and troubleshooting at companies like Digital Ocean. Traversal is already in production at Digital Ocean with a measured 40% MTTR reduction. The talk integrates causal ML, agent swarms, and production-scale observability infrastructure requiring advanced understanding. Recorded conference presentation at AI Engineer World's Fair. All evidence anchors are graded as said_in_transcript with direct excerpts from the transcript.

summary: Agarwal identifies three pillars of software engineering: system design, development, and troubleshooting. While AI tools like Cursor and Copilot streamline development, troubleshooting remains unsolved and will worsen as AI-written code reduces human context and systems grow more complex. Current workflows involve dashboard dumpster diving across Grafana, DataDog, Splunk, and Sentry, then escalating to large Slack channels. Three existing AI/ML approaches fail fundamentally: AIOps statistical anomaly detection produces too many false positives; LLMs cannot handle terabyte-scale telemetry and lack numerical understanding; ReAct-style agents depend on deprecated runbooks and are too slow for 2-5 minute resolution windows. Traversal combines causal machine learning to distinguish root causes from correlated failures, semantic reasoning models to extract rich context from logs and code, and a novel agentic control flow using swarms of agents with thousands of parallel tool calls for exhaustive telemetry search. The agent swarm and causal ML together find promising leads from seas of information, connect them to specific code changes such as pull requests, and pull in the right teams with the right context at the right time. Matt Schoenbauer presents a Digital Ocean case study showing 40% MTTR reduction. In the post-Traversal workflow, an ambient AI begins investigation with the same limited context engineers receive, orchestrates swarms of expert agents to sift through petabytes of observability data in parallel, and returns findings in about five minutes directly in the incident Slack channel. The Traversal UI cites relevant observability data, provides confidence levels for root cause candidates, explains reasoning, offers AI-generated impact maps, and supports follow-up questions. Schoenbauer notes the problem extends beyond observability to network observability and cybersecurity, framing it as both an AI agents and AI infrastructure problem—a needle-in-a-haystack search across trillions of logs and thousands of services in heterogeneous enterprise environments.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction: The Three Pillars of Software Engineering
sections.summary: Agarwal frames software engineering as three pillars: system design, development, and troubleshooting. AI tools are narrowing the development phase, raising the hope that engineers can focus on creative system design work, but he believes troubleshooting will actually consume most of engineers' time instead.

sections.title: The Worsening Problem of Troubleshooting
sections.summary: Troubleshooting will get harder for two reasons: humans will have less context as AI writes more code, and systems will be pushed to greater complexity. The result is that most engineers will spend their time on call and QA, a grim reality if unaddressed.

sections.title: Current Troubleshooting Workflow and Its Failures
sections.summary: The current workflow involves dashboard dumpster diving through thousands of dashboards in Grafana, DataDog, Splunk, and Sentry, then connecting findings to code changes, staring at code, and escalating to large Slack incident channels. This status quo is suboptimal and worsening.

sections.title: Why Current AI/ML Solutions are Failing
sections.summary: Three existing approaches fail fundamentally: AIOps traditional ML produces too many false positives in complex systems; LLMs cannot handle terabyte-scale telemetry, lack numerical understanding, and exceed context limits; ReAct-style agents rely on immediately deprecated runbooks and are too slow for the 2-5 minute resolution window.

sections.title: Traversal.ai's Novel Approach to Autonomous Troubleshooting
sections.summary: Traversal combines causal machine learning to find cause-and-effect relationships distinguishing root causes from correlated failures, semantic reasoning models to extract rich context from logs and code, and a novel agentic control flow using swarms of agents with thousands of parallel tool calls for exhaustive telemetry search. This enables out-of-sample autonomous troubleshooting from first principles for never-before-seen incidents.

sections.title: Case Study: How Traversal.ai helped Digital Ocean
sections.summary: Schoenbauer describes his HFT background debugging production incidents and how he joined Traversal after hearing Agarwal mention causal AI for incident remediation. He presents the Digital Ocean case study: before Traversal, on-call engineers faced 40-60 person Slack channels, hundreds of millions of metrics across thousands of dashboards, tens of billions of logs from thousands of services, searching for a microscopic root cause. With Traversal, the ambient AI begins investigation using the same initial context engineers receive, orchestrates swarms of expert agents to sift through petabytes of observability data in parallel, and returns findings in about five minutes directly in Slack. Digital Ocean achieved approximately 40% MTTR reduction. The Traversal UI cites relevant data, provides confidence levels for root cause candidates, explains reasoning, offers AI-generated impact maps, and supports follow-up questions about incident impact on specific stack components.

sections.title: The Broader Vision for Traversal.ai
sections.summary: Schoenbauer explains that Traversal works across heterogeneous enterprise environments, integrating with essentially every observability tool at massive scale involving trillions of logs. He frames the problem as both an AI agents and AI infrastructure problem—a needle-in-a-haystack search for a small piece of information in a massive dataset. The exhaustive search and swarm-of-agents strategies apply beyond observability to network observability and cybersecurity. He highlights the team's composition—AI researchers from top labs, dev tools veterans, AI product engineers, and HFT quant traders—and closes with a hiring pitch.
